title: Orchestration-led interface PRD and go-live checklist for hosted generation suite
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This PRD defines the scoped behavior, acceptance criteria, and a concrete go-live checklist for the orchestration-led hosted generation suite: chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. The objective is to ship a single set of operator-visible endpoint contracts and an orchestration policy layer that enables graded fallbacks, region-aware routing, and cost/latency banding for our Hosted API customers.

Goals:
- Deliver a unified, backward-compatible API surface for generation features (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) with explicit behavior guarantees documented in the Endpoint Contract appendix.
- Provide platform operators with rollout controls: canary weight, lane-based quality SLOs, and automated fallback to compatible model variants or degraded lanes.
- Ensure performance and cost SLOs are met for P0 tenants under the default lane profile.

Non-goals:
- This scope does not include model training or onboarding new model architectures.
- No changes to client SDKs beyond optional query parameters (see API changes).
- No on-prem or VPC deployment packaging changes in this iteration.

User stories:
- As an external product engineer, I need an endpoint that returns deterministic embeddings for identical inputs so I can index user content reliably.
- As an ops engineer, I need canary controls and clear rollback triggers so I can mitigate quality regressions during rollouts.
- As a PM for a tiered customer, I need documented cost/latency bands to pick the correct lane and budget for queries.

Requirements (functional):
1) API surface: The existing generation endpoints remain; add a new optional orchestration hint header X-RW-Orch: {lane, tolerance, bailout}. The header is purely opt-in.
2) Behavioral contracts: For chat/completions, we guarantee token-level streaming compatible with the current SDK. For embeddings, similarity-preserving behavior must match the v1 embeddings policy (stability threshold >= 0.92 on reference set). For rerank, the endpoint must return stable ranking for identical candidate orderings within epsilon of previous run.
3) Fallback policy: Orchestration must support automatic fallback to: a) lower-cost quantized model with a detectable quality delta; b) regional fallback if the requested region is unavailable.
4) Observability hooks: Per-request telemetry must include model_version, lane, routing_decision, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, and cost_estimate.
5) Rollout controls: Console/CLI must enable traffic slicing by percentage, user cohort, and tenant.

Requirements (non-functional):
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile generation latency under default lane must be <= 450ms for completions up to 256 tokens.
- Throughput: Dedicated reserved compute must sustain 1200 concurrent requests / second under continuous batching profile in performance tests.
- Cost targets: Per-token unit cost for default lane should be <= 60% of current legacy-hosted baseline.
- Security/compliance: All data path events must be logged to customer audit logs when tenant opt-in is enabled. KMS-integrated key management must be available for Private deployments (note: out-of-scope for current rollout but a dependency).

API changes (summary):
- Support header X-RW-Orch with enum values for lane (default|economy|latency|premium), tolerance (high|med|low), bailout (auto|manual).
- New /orchestration/status endpoint for operators to introspect rollout state and active lane metrics (read-only for customers).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Functional acceptance: Each endpoint (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) passes the behavior conformance suite with zero critical failures against the baseline test corpus.
- Performance acceptance: Benchmark runs in the staging performance cluster demonstrate meeting latency and throughput SLOs at 90% load and sustained 60% load.
- Observability acceptance: Telemetry fields (model_version, lane, routing_decision, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, cost_estimate) appear in traces and dashboards and are queryable in the Console within 10 minutes of ingestion.
- Rollout acceptance: Console canary can be configured to 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% with automated health checks that will pause promotion on SLA or quality regressions.
- Security acceptance: Security review sign-off recorded and SSO gating enabled for operator controls; all audit events emitted to the tenant audit stream for test tenants.

Launch readiness checklist (pre-launch tasks):
- [ ] Finalize Endpoint Contract docs in Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/HostedGen/EndpointContract)
- [ ] Merge orchestration service PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestration/pull/412, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/889
- [ ] Integration test run 5 consecutive clean runs in staging: test-run-2026-03-01..03 (dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/staging/hosted-gen)
- [ ] Performance sign-off from infra benchmarks run 2026-03-08 (artifact: s3://redwood-benchmarks/2026-03-hosted-gen/index.html)
- [ ] Console feature flags and canary controls reviewed by UX and Security
- [ ] E2E observability validated: traces, logs, metrics, and cost telemetry flowing to Console (playbook step IDs: OBS-22, OBS-23)
- [ ] Customer-facing docs drafted and reviewed (docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/254)
- [ ] Runbook and rollback plan finalized with on-call rota updated

Launch play (day-of):
1) Create canary at 1% with passive scoring enabled for quality and latency thresholds.
2) Monitor the canary dashboard for 30 minutes; automated hooks to notify on-call Slack channel (#oncall-hosted-gen).
3) If canary stable, promote to 5% for 60 minutes; run a small synthetic traffic sweep (queries from synthetic-user cohort A).
4) If stable, promote to 25% with a 3-hour observation window, execute additional long-tail latency sampling.
5) Full promotion to 100% only after runbook sign-off by Product, SWE on-call, and Reliability engineers.

Rollback criteria and actions:
- Immediate rollback trigger if: >2% increase in error rate above baseline, >20% degradation in similarity score for embeddings reference set, or P50 latency regression >30% from baseline for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Rollback action: Route all traffic to previous stable model variant and lane, increase logging level to debug for 15 minutes, and create incident ticket with priority P0.

Open questions and clarifications required:
- Should the orchestration header be accepted from SDKs by default or opt-in via the Console? (PM decision pending)
- Final tolerance-to-lane mapping for rerank endpoints (quantify acceptable ranking drift).
- Acceptance threshold for 'cost_estimate' telemetry sampling frequency (per-request vs. aggregated).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regression when falling back to quantized models. Mitigation: Add post-fallback sanity checks using a lightweight eval harness; escalate to manual rollback if delta exceeds threshold.
- Risk: Hidden cost overhead from orchestration logic. Mitigation: Run a 7-day cost simulation with representative traffic and include cost-estimate telemetry in dashboards.

Decisions log (summary):
- 2026-03-10: Agreed on header-based opt-in orchestration hints to avoid breaking existing clients. (Decision owner: Aisha)
- 2026-03-12: Chose stability threshold 0.92 for embeddings conformance tests after trade-off discussion with Research. (Decision owner: Research lead)

Comments and recent updates (chronological):
- 2026-03-14: Liam O'Connor: Initial PRD draft completed; flagged dependency on ENG-4899 (kv-cache telemetry schema).
- 2026-03-15: Reliability review (notes): identified potential hotspot in kernel scheduler when batching collides with lane-specific priorities; engineering to prototype scheduling knob (ENG-5021).
- 2026-03-15: Docs PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/254 (Aisha)
- 2026-03-15: UX request: add a small help tooltip to Console canary slider describing quality checks. (Design follow-up DES-3321)
